_readme: Deterministic demo scripts. Paste these verbatim to rehearse the video — each has a predicted engine outcome so the demo is repeatable. Verified against the engine on 2026-07-23.

photosynthesis.label: memorized
photosynthesis.expected: parrot flag TRUE, textbook similarity ~100%, phrase overlap ~100%, label 'memorized'
photosynthesis.text: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants and some other organisms use sunlight to synthesise food from carbon dioxide and water. In the presence of chlorophyll and sunlight, carbon dioxide and water are converted into glucose and oxygen.

photosynthesis.label: partial
photosynthesis.use_for: Loop Mode BEFORE — gaps are real and closable
photosynthesis.expected: score ~70, label 'partial', gaps include co2_intake / water_uptake / oxygen_byproduct
photosynthesis.text: Basically the plant uses sunlight to make its own food. The green stuff in the leaves grabs the light and that energy is used to turn air and water into sugar for the plant.

photosynthesis.label: good
photosynthesis.use_for: Loop Mode AFTER — the +delta money shot
photosynthesis.expected: score ~89, label 'good', coverage ~0.82, no parrot flag
photosynthesis.text: Sunlight hits the leaf and chlorophyll, the green pigment, soaks up that energy. The roots pull water up from the soil while tiny holes called stomata let carbon dioxide in from the air. Inside the chloroplasts that energy rearranges the water and carbon dioxide into glucose, which is the sugar the plant stores as food. Oxygen is left over and gets released into the air.

photosynthesis.label: wrong
photosynthesis.use_for: 'You said X — but actually Y' card
photosynthesis.expected: label 'wrong', wrongStatement flags the soil misconception
photosynthesis.text: Plants get their food from the soil through their roots. The leaves breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide to make energy for the plant.

newtons_laws.label: partial
newtons_laws.use_for: Gap detection that is obvious to a human judge
newtons_laws.expected: score ~82, gap 'third_law_pairs' — the student never mentions action-reaction
newtons_laws.text: If nothing pushes an object it just keeps doing what it was doing. If you push something heavy it speeds up slower than something light, because force is mass times acceleration.

newtons_laws.label: good
newtons_laws.text: An object sitting still stays still and a moving object keeps moving straight at the same speed unless some unbalanced force acts on it. That resistance to a change in motion is inertia. How fast it speeds up depends on the force divided by the mass, so force equals mass times acceleration, and a heavier object needs a bigger push for the same acceleration. Also every push comes in a pair. If I push a wall the wall pushes back on me just as hard in the opposite direction, and because those two forces act on different objects they do not cancel each other out.

respiration.label: partial
respiration.use_for: Explain Mode — persona asks about ATP
respiration.text: Respiration is how cells get energy out of food. Glucose gets broken down using oxygen and that releases energy the cell can use, and carbon dioxide comes out as waste.

respiration.label: wrong
respiration.text: Respiration is just breathing in and out. It happens in the lungs where air goes in and out of the body to make energy.

cell_structure.label: partial
cell_structure.use_for: Viva Mode — examiner pushes on the nucleus
cell_structure.text: A cell is the smallest unit of a living thing. It has a membrane around the outside that controls what goes in and out, and inside there is cytoplasm and a nucleus that runs the cell.

atoms_molecules.label: good
atoms_molecules.text: An atom is the tiniest bit of an element that still counts as that element. In the middle there is a nucleus holding protons which are positive and neutrons which have no charge, and electrons which are negative move around the outside. Because there are the same number of protons and electrons the whole atom ends up neutral. When two or more atoms bond together you get a molecule, and if those atoms are from different elements like hydrogen and oxygen in water then it is a compound.

reflection_light.label: partial
reflection_light.use_for: Depth round — 'why measure from the normal?'
reflection_light.text: Reflection is when light bounces off something instead of going through it. The angle it comes in at is the same as the angle it bounces off at, and that is measured from the normal line.
